<!-- pr-reviewer: f7dde671eac8e1e1e1daf3f660fda92a1e13b0d5 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good
- `stack_span.rs` gives (c2) and (d2) one z-span rule. The window only grows against the old one, and a level move reduces to the old sums, so old verdicts cannot be dropped.
- Strict-dip silences are preserved. Every band is still judged by the existing strict `band_hits_box`. A retract off a mounting face, a plunge onto one, a traverse riding one and flush contact keep the tip at or above the steel, so they stay silent. `the_strict_dip_silences_hold_for_the_whole_stack` pins this, including the 0.001 penetration that must report.
- The upright-rapid stack comes from `upper_bands(tool, holder, spindle)` over the same `HolderStack` that (c2) and the posed sweep take (`laws.rs`, the `upper` binding in `rapids_vs_fixtures_held`). `an_upright_rapid_reads_a_modelled_holder_bodys_bands` pins the modelled body (a slim r5 clears, the r20 collar hits).
- A non-finite z fails closed (NaN window counts as a hit). No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`, and the provenance line is present.
- The flute disc is checked first and still reports `Rapid`, so existing verdicts keep their labels. The decisions file is in place, and the body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #424` / `Fixes #425`.
- `laws.rs` shrinks from 392 to 349 lines.

## Local results (merged with current upstream/main; clean merge, no conflicts)
No `build.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `.github` or scripts changes, so it was built.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| sim `fixture_stack_span` | 8 passed |
| app `fixture_law_gaps` | 3 passed |
| app `fixtures` | 14 passed |
| app `rotary_fixtures` | 4 passed |
| app `tool_body` | 8 passed |
| app `posting` | 17 passed |
| app `turning_holder` | 8 passed |
| app `carried_fixtures_cache` | 6 passed |
| sim `posed_fixture` | 7 passed |
| sim `posed_fixture_midpose` | 3 passed |
| sim `posed_rapids` | 5 passed |
| sim `sideways_rapids` | 3 passed |
| sim `radial_rapids` | 15 passed |
| sim `vertical_rapids` | 16 passed |
| sim `--lib` | 62 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- On long ramps the enclosing window can over-report a graze. This is the stated, fail-safe trade-off, documented in the module header and the decisions file.
- With #430 (fixture mesh) an upright-rapid holder hit may read as `Rapid`. This is a label difference only, and the post is blocked either way.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f7dde671eac8e1e1e1daf3f660fda92a1e13b0d5 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- One shared rule for the tool stack's z span (`crates/sim/src/verify/stack_span.rs`), used by both law c2 and law d2. The window only grows against the old one, and a level move keeps the old arithmetic, so no existing verdict is dropped.
- A non-finite z fails closed as a hit, and the strict-dip silences are kept (retract off a face, plunge onto a face, flush contact).
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new module. It carries a provenance header and stays well under 400 lines. `laws.rs` shrinks (349 lines).
- Tests pin both gaps: 8 sim tests and 3 app tests, including the `posting::verification_gate` refusal. Body ends `Fixes #424` / `Fixes #425` and has a `Changelog:` line. The decisions file is per-PR and `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched. No build.rs, scripts, workflow or dependency changes.

**Local results (merged with current main; trial merge was clean)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| sim fixture_stack_span | 8 passed |
| sim vertical_rapids / posed_fixture / posed_fixture_midpose / posed_rapids / sideways_rapids / radial_rapids | 16 / 7 / 3 / 5 / 3 / 15 passed |
| app fixture_law_gaps | 3 passed |
| app fixtures / rotary_fixtures / tool_body / posting | 14 / 4 / 8 / 17 passed |
| app turning_holder / drilling_cross_holder / drilling_cross_rapids / turning_axial_rapids / carried_fixtures_cache | 8 / 2 / 2 / 3 / 6 passed |
| clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The enclosing window can over-report a graze on a long ramp. The PR and decisions file state this trade-off openly, and it errs toward refusing the post, never toward missing a crash.
- Per the PR text, a meshed fixture (#430) will read an upright-rapid holder hit as `Rapid` rather than `Holder`. That is a label difference only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
